messages:
Priya R: heads-up — starting UmbraFlux (customer Delta) LoRA merge onboarding. pushed branch umbrafux/cust-delta-lora into staging. quick smoke showed a numeric token shift for invoice amounts. attaching evalpack in gdrive :link:
Danielle M: on it. can you drop the evalpack name and top failing prompt?
Priya R: evalpack: cust-delta-invoice-smokepack-v1. top failing prompt id 0172: 'Total due: $12,345.67' model returns '12,345' (loses cents) about 23% of cases during long-context runs.
Matt K: hmm tokenizer mismatch maybe? Did we remap special tokens from their finetune?
Priya R: checked their merge script — they used default tokenizer mapping. LoRA was trained with a tokenization patch (cust_delta_tok_v2). merge didn't include that. suspect token id drift when quantizing to int4.
Sanjeev: ok plan: 1) run tokenmap diff between base and cust tok v2, 2) run smoke eval on floating fp16 to isolate quant noise, 3) run int4 quant with and without remap to see delta. I can run 2 & 3 on dedicated test slot later today.
Danielle M: I can do 1. quick diff: `python3 tools/tokenmap_diff.py --base models/umbra-base/tokenizer.json --other customer/tokenizers/cust_delta_tok_v2.json`
Danielle M: output snippet:
```
@@
- "$": 345
+ "$": 1023
- ".": 56
+ ".": 512
@@
```
Danielle M: looks like some punctuation token ids shifted — that will change byte-level inputs to KV cache indexing.
Matt K: good catch. if token ids differ, a direct LoRA patch apply will anchor to wrong embeddings -> numeric collapse.
Priya R: exactly. propose rebase step: during merge we remap LoRA's token id references to cust tok v2. There's a small script in our repo: `scripts/rebase_lora_tokenids.py` — use with `--target-tokenizer customer/tokenizers/cust_delta_tok_v2.json`.
Sanjeev: I'll run fp16 smoke first to confirm baseline. command I'll run: `./bench/run_quick_eval.sh --model umbrafux-lora-staged --quant none --prompts evalpacks/cust-delta-invoice-smokepack-v1 --out /tmp/umbra_fp16.json`
Priya R: sounds good. after that run two quant variants: `--quant int4` and `--quant int4 --apply-token-remap scripts/cust-delta-remap.json` so we can compare.
EvalBot: quick-eval job started (job id ej-99231) — running on dedicated-gpu-6. ETA ~12m. :eyes:
Matt K: also add a short unit test in our smoketest harness: assert cents preserved for currency prompts. should fail now, pass after remap.
Danielle M: added test at tests/smoke/currency_cents.test — small PR incoming.
Sanjeev: fp16 run finished. summary: cents preserved 98.7% fp16 (baseline), int4 without remap 74.1%, int4 with remap 96.4%. logs: `/mnt/results/ej-99231/summary.json`
Priya R: great numbers — confirms token id remap recovers most of the quality. can we automate remap during merge so customers don't hit this?
Matt K: yes add an extra merge step in the adapter onboarding pipeline: detect tokenizer differences, produce mapping, apply to LoRA weight keys that reference embedding index. fallback flag `--skip-remap` for advanced users.
Priya R: will draft PR for onboarding pipeline change + docs for customers. tagging @Matt K to review.
Danielle M: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/adapter-onboard/pull/421 — includes script, test, and a short note in docs/onboarding.md
Priya R: thanks all. follow-up: after merge I'll run the full cust smokepack (800 prompts) and schedule a dedicated-run for night to validate rollout. ops-bot, please reserve dedicated-gpu-6 between 02:00-04:00 UTC.
ops-bot: reservation confirmed for dedicated-gpu-6 at 2025-05-21T02:00:00Z to 2025-05-21T04:00:00Z — reservation id res-74411
Matt K: nice. one more thing — add a small note in the release checklist to run tokenmap diff for any customer finetune that supplies a tokenizer. saved us. :thumbsup:
